headline: Iran discusses with Qatar normalising traffic in Hormuz, but flow remains reduced
summary: Iran and Qatar are negotiating to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but shipping flow through the waterway remains reduced. Iranian demands are part of the talks.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil and LNG shipping chokepoints, so disruptions there feed directly into global energy prices and supply.
why_moved: Reduced flow through the Strait of Hormuz limits oil and gas supply. Talks on normalising traffic leave the outcome uncertain, which supports energy price risk.
